title: [YouPass Collect] - Top 200 Universities Comparisons in 2011
prompt: The table shows the number of universities ranked in the top 200 in the world (2011) in three subjects in five countries. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the number of universities from five countries that were ranked among the top 200 globally in three academic disciplines in 2011.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the United States had by far the highest representation across all three subjects, while New Zealand recorded the lowest figures. In addition, Biology attracted the most universities to the top 200 ranking, whereas Medicine had the fewest.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the leading nations, American universities dominated the rankings, with 69 institutions listed in Biology, which was 11 higher than Psychology, at 58. Medicine had a slightly lower figure of 54 universities. Meanwhile, the UK came second across all disciplines, with 30 universities ranked in Biology, close to the Psychology figure of 29, while Medicine had 24 institutions in the top 200.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining countries, Australia had 9 universities ranked in Biology, identical to Canada's figure for the same subject. However, Australia had slightly more institutions in Medicine and Psychology, at 13 and 17 respectively, compared to Canada's 12 and 14. Finally, New Zealand had the weakest presence, with only 6 universities in Biology and 4 in Psychology. Notably, Medicine recorded a particularly low figure of just 2 institutions, making it the least represented country across all three academic fields.
